label: Blue Note (BLP 1593)
rationale: Lou Donaldson's 'undisputed masterpiece' (Steve Huey, AllMusic) — recorded July 28, 1958 at Van Gelder Studio, Hackensack with Herman Foster (piano), Peck Morrison (bass), Dave Bailey (drums) and Ray Barretto (congas); released on Blue Note as BLP 1593. Huey: the album 'marks the point where the altoist began to decisively modify his heavy Charlie Parker influence and add a smoky, bluesy flavor of his own,' with the title cut 'a classic, arguably Donaldson's signature tune.' AllMusic 5 stars, Penguin Guide 2.5 (as reported by Wikipedia). The canon's Donaldson row currently starts at Alligator Bogaloo (1967); this is the earlier defining statement and a load-bearing link in the grooving hard-bop lineage — the Blues Walk / Move / Play Ray / Callin' All Cats repertoire that would go on to harden into soul jazz.

personnel_record.notes: Single session, full quintet on all six tracks. AllMusic's header lists the recording location as 'New York, NY' (S1); jazzdisco (#580728) and Wikipedia document Van Gelder Studio, Hackensack, NJ — the studio's Hackensack era runs through mid-1959, and the session matrix numbers BLP 1593 (also issued as 45-1720 Blues Walk/The Masquerade Is Over and 45-1721 Play Ray/Autumn Nocturne) corroborate the date. Alfred Lion producer, Rudy Van Gelder recording engineer and mastering, Francis Wolff cover photography, Ira Gitler liner notes (S2 technical personnel). Style: AllMusic styles it Hard Bop and Huey places it in Donaldson's 'early, pre-soul-jazz period'; the blues-and-conga gravity of the title cut is the lineage point toward the soul jazz of the 1960s. Apple's copy (725829554, 1987 CD) carries the six original tracks.

ballot.case_for: Blues Walk is Donaldson's undisputed masterpiece (Huey, AllMusic, 5 stars) — the album where he decisively moved beyond his Parker influence into the blues-drenched, groove-oriented identity that would define his career, with the title track standing as 'arguably Donaldson's signature tune' (S1). The lineage argument is the strongest signal here: the conga-enhanced groove and the Blues Walk / Play Ray / Callin' All Cats repertoire form the load-bearing bridge between 1950s hard-bop and the 1960s soul-jazz the canon already carries via Alligator Bogaloo (1967) — Barretto's addition is the audible hinge, called 'a subtle masterstroke' by Huey. A canon row that begins at the soul-jazz crossover without the originating hard-bop statement is lopsided, and a curious listener sent to the title track cold would immediately hear what makes the idiom inviting.
ballot.case_against: The consensus is thin at the top tier: Penguin Guide 2.5 (as reported by S2) is 'well worth having' but not Crown, and the dossier carries no NPR, DownBeat, JazzTimes, or musician-citation evidence — the cross-tradition listing the rubric weights highest is simply absent, leaving AllMusic as the sole critical voice at 5 stars. Session gravity is modest: a cohesive working quintet at Van Gelder, not the all-star cross-pollination (Morgan, Blakey, Silver) that defines the era's absolute must-haves, and the 1958 Blue Note hard-bop shelf is already densely populated with peers whose canonical claims are deeper. Donaldson is a respected bandleader but not a first-tier architect of the idiom, and the soul-jazz bridge argument — while real — does not by itself overwhelm the thinness of the multi-source consensus.
ballot.disagreement: The references split on tier: one reads the defining-statement and lineage evidence as consensus_core, judging the for-case overwhelming despite the Penguin 2.5; the other reads the thin top-tier consensus, modest session gravity, and period redundancy as a real case both ways — contested. Both converge on priority: strong.
ballot.recommendation: The council proposes Blues Walk as a strong contested candidate — the soul-jazz bridge and Donaldson's defining statement earn it genuine consideration, but John should weigh whether the one-critic-deep 5-star consensus and modest session gravity warrant the slot against the denser 1958 hard-bop peers already in or approaching the canon.
